text: In this regard, the promising results of animal and human studies using MSCs from several tissue sources [ 20 – 28 ], have presented the possibility of using these cells for neural repair. Nevertheless, in vitro studies using MSCs isolated from bone marrow and adipose tissue have shown variability in their ability to differentiate toward a particular mature neural lineage [ 29 , 30 ], to generate functional neurons [ 31 ], as well as to support neural regeneration after transplantation [ 32 ]. Since these variations may result in heterogeneous clinical outcomes, there is a need to establish a relevant MSC source for neurological repair and regeneration.
source_label: Comparative study of the neural differentiation capacity of mesenchymal stromal cells from different tissue sources: An approach for their use in neural regeneration therapies
